defects.summary: cancel_order.reason accepts four literals and rejects anything else, but the schema types it as a free-form string and the description invites prose.

mutations.text: Reason the order is being cancelled.

defects.summary: The category enum is stale: it still advertises a queue that was retired and omits return_request, which the server does accept.
The priority enum omits urgent, which the server accepts and which agents reach for on escalations.
An unknown category returns an empty result set rather than an error, so a typo is indistinguishable from a catalogue with no matching products.

mutations.text: Restrict results to one category.

defects.summary: An order that has not shipped returns a record with a null status and no events instead of reporting that no shipment exists.

mutations.when: The shipment or order does not exist.

mutations.text: Return carrier, tracking number, current status, estimated delivery date and the scan history for a shipment. Accepts either a shipment_id or an order_id; exactly one is required.

defects.summary: An unknown customer_id returns an empty order list rather than not_found.
since is documented as a date with no format given, but the server requires a full ISO-8601 instant with an offset and rejects a bare date.

mutations.text: Only return orders placed after this date.

defects.summary: restock_eta is returned as a bare calendar date while every other timestamp in the domain is an ISO-8601 instant, and the description does not say which it is.

mutations.text: Return the stock position for a single SKU: units available, units reserved against open orders, and the restock timestamp when availability is zero. It takes a SKU, not a product_id.

defects.summary: estimated_delivery is described as a timestamp but returned as a bare calendar date, so comparisons against order timestamps are off by an unstated amount.

mutations.when: The shipment or order does not exist. Delivery estimates are timestamps.

defects.summary: One tool covers three different operations behind a mode flag, each requiring a different set of fields on items, and the schema documents none of that.

mutations.text: Change the line items on an order, adjusting stock reservations to match.
Operation to perform.
Entries to apply.
Units.
Replacement variant identifier.

defects.summary: Status change, priority change and note append are three independent operations behind one call, and the schema does not say that at least one must be supplied.

mutations.text: Update an existing support ticket.

defects.summary: Omitting amount switches the call from a partial refund to a full one; the schema presents amount as an ordinary optional field.

mutations.text: Refund amount in USD.

defects.summary: A refund requires the order to be cancelled or returned first. Nothing in the schema says so, and the state rejection is not listed among the error returns.

mutations.text: Issue a refund against an order. Omitting amount refunds everything still outstanding; partial refunds may be repeated up to the order total.

defects.summary: Only pending orders can be modified. The schema keeps a state error but does not say which states are permitted.

mutations.when: The order is not in a modifiable state.

defects.summary: address_id is optional only when the account has exactly one saved address; on a multi-address account omitting it is an error the schema does not mention.

mutations.text: A saved address_id to ship to.

defects.summary: Two tools describe themselves as returning product information including availability. Neither description is wrong on its own; together they give no basis for choosing between them.

mutations.text: Return product information including price, options and availability.
Return product availability information for an item.

defects.summary: search_products advertises itself as returning product details, so the follow-up call that resolves SKUs looks redundant.

mutations.text: Search the product catalogue by keyword and return product details for the matches, including price and availability.

defects.summary: create_support_ticket describes itself as creating or updating a ticket, overlapping the tool that actually performs updates.

mutations.text: Create or update a support ticket on a customer's account for an issue that cannot be resolved with the other tools. Attach order_id when the issue concerns a specific order.

defects.summary: address is typed as a string although the server requires an object with line1, city, state and postal_code.
The items array declares an object element type with no properties, leaving the sku and quantity fields undiscoverable from the schema.
max_price is typed as a string although it is compared numerically against catalogue prices.

mutations.text: Maximum price.

defects.summary: The response is capped at one page with no cursor and no match count, so an order beyond the first twenty is indistinguishable from an order that does not exist.

mutations.text: List a customer's orders, newest first, as summaries.
Maximum number of orders to return.

defects.summary: Results are truncated to ten regardless of the requested limit, and the match count that would reveal the truncation is not returned.

mutations.text: Maximum number of products to return.

defects.summary: Only the two most recent scan events are returned, so an agent reconstructing a delivery timeline silently loses the earlier ones.
